questions.text:
Part 1 (18 marks)
Write the output of each Python expression.
Each subquestion is worth 2 marks. To get full marks you must specify both the correct value and be clear in your answer that you understand what the type will be. If you think an expression is not legal according to the rules of Python, you should writeErrorin the box.
" hello world ".strip().upper()
[x % 3 for x in range(1, 5)]

Part 2 (16 marks)
For each subquestion, give asinglePython assignment statement.
Each subquestion is worth 4 marks. If your answer uses more than one assignment statement, you will receive 0 marks
Given a list values of integers, write one line of code to assign has_zero the value True if any element equals zero, otherwise False.
Given a string s, assign to t the result of replacing all spaces in s with hyphens '-'.
Suppose that data is a Python dictionary where all values are unique and hashable. Assign to swapped a new dictionary where the original values become keys and the original keys become values.

Suppose that password is a Python string. Assign to secure_pw a new string where every vowel ('a', 'e', 'i', 'o', 'u', case-insensitive) is replaced with '*', and all other characters remain unchanged.

Part 3 (8 marks)
Select the correct response(s) to each of the subquestions below. Each of the questions below is worth two marks.
Which conversions will raise an error? (Select all that apply)
Which operations will NOT raise an error? (Select all that apply)
Which of the following create the dictionary {1: 1, 2: 4, 3: 9}? (Select all that apply)
Which statements about Python functions are true? (Select all that apply)
